/-!
# Overfull conjecture

The *overfull conjecture* of Chetwynd and Hilton (1986): a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$
vertices with maximum degree $\Delta(G) > n/3$ is class 2 if and only if it has an overfull
subgraph $S$ with $\Delta(S) = \Delta(G)$.

A finite graph $H$ is *overfull* if $|E(H)| > \Delta(H) \lfloor |V(H)|/2 \rfloor$. A graph $G$ is
*class 2* if its chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ (the least number of colours in a proper edge
colouring) equals $\Delta(G) + 1$. By Vizing's theorem, $\chi'(G)$ is always $\Delta(G)$ or
$\Delta(G) + 1$.

The Wikipedia list entry writes the hypothesis as $\Delta(G) \geq n/3$. We follow the original
paper and the Wikipedia article on overfull graphs, which use the strict bound $\Delta(G) > n/3$.
The bound cannot be relaxed: the Petersen graph with one vertex deleted ($n = 9$, $\Delta = 3$)
is class 2 but has no overfull subgraph $S$ with $\Delta(S) = 3$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Overfull graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overfull_graph%23Overfull_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. G. Chetwynd, A. J. W. Hilton, *Star multigraphs with three vertices of maximum degree*,
  Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 100 (1986), 303–317.
  [doi:10.1017/S030500410006610X](https://doi.org/10.1017/S030500410006610X)
-/

claims.decomposer_note: Single Prop over finite simple graphs G with n = |V(G)|: 'class 2' means chromatic index Δ(G)+1 (i.e. not Δ(G)-edge-colourable, so Δ(G) ≥ 1 is implicitly needed), 'overfull' means |E(S)| > Δ(S)·⌊|V(S)|/2⌋ for a (not necessarily induced) subgraph S; the list entry writes the hypothesis as Δ(G) ≥ n/3 while the article and the original Chetwynd–Hilton (1986) conjecture use the strict Δ(G) > n/3 (the bound should be handled as a real/rational inequality, not natural-number division); the 'if' direction is a known easy fact, so the conjectural content is the 'only if' direction, but the statement poses the biconditional as one claim.
claims.reviewer_why: c08's declaration (identical in substance to c03/c05/c06) is used: finite simple graph G on a Fintype V, hypothesis (card V : ℝ)/3 < Δ(G) (strict, real inequality), conclusion IsClassTwo G ↔ ∃ S : G.Subgraph, IsOverfull S.coe ∧ S.coe.maxDegree = G.maxDegree, where IsClassTwo is χ'(G) = Δ(G)+1 with χ' = chromaticNumber of Mathlib's lineGraph, and IsOverfull is Δ·⌊|V|/2⌋ < |E| (ℕ floor division) evaluated on the subgraph's own vertex set. Edits: explicit [DecidableRel G.Adj] on G (as in c03/c05), tests merged from c03/c06/c08. c01/c02/c04/c07 were rejected because they formalize the list entry's literal non-strict bound Δ(G) ≥ n/3, which I verified by brute force is a false statement (Petersen graph minus a vertex: n = 9, Δ = 3, class 2, no overfull subgraph with Δ(S) = 3); the actual open conjecture (article + Chetwynd–Hilton 1986) uses the strict bound.
claims.source_text: a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G) \geq n/3$ is class 2 if and only if it has an overfull subgraph $S$ satisfying $\Delta(S) = \Delta(G)$
claims.text_span: a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G) \geq n/3$ is class 2 if and only if it has an overfull subgraph $S$ satisfying $\Delta(S) = \Delta(G)$

context: In graph theory, an overfull graph is a graph whose size is greater than the product of its maximum degree and half of its order floored, i.e. $|E|>\Delta (G)\lfloor |V|/2\rfloor$ where $|E|$ is the size of G, $\displaystyle \Delta (G)$ is the maximum degree of G, and $|V|$ is the order of G. The concept of an overfull subgraph, an overfull graph that is a subgraph, immediately follows. An alternate, stricter definition of an overfull subgraph S of a graph G requires $\displaystyle \Delta (G)=\Delta (S)$.

decomposition_objections.text: The list-entry text writes the hypothesis as Δ(G) ≥ n/3, but the table notes themselves record that the Wikipedia article and the original Chetwynd–Hilton (1986) paper use the strict bound Δ(G) > n/3. The non-strict version is actually false: the Petersen graph minus one vertex has n = 9, Δ = 3 (so Δ = n/3 exactly), is class 2 (a 3-edge-colouring of P − v would extend to a 1-factorization of the Petersen graph), and has no overfull subgraph S with Δ(S) = 3 (the only candidate odd orders 5, 7, 9 would need ≥ 7, ≥ 10, ≥ 13 edges respectively, impossible since P − v has 12 edges, girth 5 and minimum degree 2). Since a `research open` statement must be the actual conjecture rather than a refuted misquote, I formalized the strict inequality and documented the discrepancy in the module docstring. If the harness insists on the literal ≥, replace `(Fintype.card V : ℝ) / 3 < G.maxDegree` by `(Fintype.card V : ℝ) / 3 ≤ G.maxDegree`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Overfull conjecture

The *overfull conjecture* of Chetwynd and Hilton (1986): a finite simple graph $G$ on $n$
vertices with maximum degree $\Delta(G) > n/3$ is class 2 if and only if it has an overfull
subgraph $S$ with $\Delta(S) = \Delta(G)$.

A finite graph $H$ is *overfull* if $|E(H)| > \Delta(H) \lfloor |V(H)|/2 \rfloor$. A graph $G$ is
*class 2* if its chromatic index $\chi'(G)$ (the least number of colours in a proper edge

$\Delta(G) + 1$.

The Wikipedia list entry writes the hypothesis as $\Delta(G) \geq n/3$. We follow the original
paper and the Wikipedia article on overfull graphs, which use the strict bound $\Delta(G) > n/3$.
The bound cannot be relaxed: the Petersen graph with one vertex deleted ($n = 9$, $\Delta = 3$)
is class 2 but has no overfull subgraph $S$ with $\Delta(S) = 3$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Overfull graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overfull_graph%23Overfull_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- A. G. Chetwynd, A. J. W. Hilton, *Star multigraphs with three vertices of maximum degree*,
  Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc. 100 (1986), 303–317.
  [doi:10.1017/S030500410006610X](https://doi.org/10.1017/S030500410006610X)
-/

namespace OverfullConjecture

open SimpleGraph

/-- The *chromatic index* $\chi'(G)$ of `G`: the least number of colours in a proper edge
colouring of `G`, i.e. the chromatic number of the line graph of `G`. -/
noncomputable def chromaticIndex {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ :=
  G.lineGraph.chromaticNumber

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V]

/-- A finite simple graph `G` is *overfull* if $|E(G)| > \Delta(G) \lfloor |V(G)| / 2 \rfloor$.
Here `Fintype.card V / 2` is natural-number division, i.e. the floor of $|V(G)| / 2$. -/
def IsOverfull [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  G.maxDegree * (Fintype.card V / 2) < G.edgeFinset.card

/-- A finite simple graph `G` is *class 2* if its chromatic index is $\Delta(G) + 1$. -/
def IsClassTwo (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Prop :=
  chromaticIndex G = G.maxDegree + 1

/-- The graph with no edges is not overfull. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isOverfull_bot [DecidableEq V] : ¬ IsOverfull (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  simp [IsOverfull]

/-- The triangle is overfull: it has $3$ edges and $\Delta \lfloor n/2 \rfloor = 2 \cdot 1 = 2$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isOverfull_top_fin_three : IsOverfull (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  unfold IsOverfull
  decide

/-- The complete graph $K_4$ is not overfull: it has $6$ edges and
$\Delta \lfloor n/2 \rfloor = 3 \cdot 2 = 6$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isOverfull_top_fin_four : ¬ IsOverfull (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 4)) := by
  unfold IsOverfull
  decide

/-- The graph with no edges is not class 2: its chromatic index is $0$ while
$\Delta + 1 = 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isClassTwo_bot : ¬ IsClassTwo (⊥ : SimpleGraph V) := by
  have : IsEmpty (⊥ : SimpleGraph V).edgeSet := by simp [isEmpty_subtype]
  simp [IsClassTwo, chromaticIndex, chromaticNumber_eq_zero_of_isEmpty]

/-- The triangle is class 2: its chromatic index is $3 = \Delta + 1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem isClassTwo_top_fin_three : IsClassTwo (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) := by
  have h : (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).lineGraph = ⊤ := by
    ext ⟨e₁, he₁⟩ ⟨e₂, he₂⟩
    simp only [lineGraph_adj_iff_exists, top_adj, ne_eq, Subtype.mk.injEq, and_iff_left_iff_imp]
    intro hne
    revert e₁ e₂
    decide
  simp only [IsClassTwo, chromaticIndex, h, chromaticNumber_top]
  have : Fintype.card (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)).edgeSet = 3 := by
    rw [← Set.toFinset_card]; decide
  rw [this]
  decide

open scoped Classical in
/-- **Overfull conjecture** (Chetwynd–Hilton, 1986).

A finite simple graph $G$ on $n$ vertices with maximum degree $\Delta(G) > n/3$ is class 2
(that is, its chromatic index is $\Delta(G) + 1$) if and only if it has an overfull subgraph
$S$ (that is, $|E(S)| > \Delta(S) \lfloor |V(S)|/2 \rfloor$) satisfying
$\Delta(S) = \Delta(G)$.

The subgraph $S$ is not required to be induced or spanning. The "if" direction is a known
elementary fact; the "only if" direction is the open part of the conjecture. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem overfull_conjecture (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hG : (Fintype.card V : ℝ) / 3 < G.maxDegree) :
    IsClassTwo G ↔
      ∃ S : G.Subgraph, IsOverfull S.coe ∧ S.coe.maxDegree = G.maxDegree := by
  sorry

end OverfullConjecture

items: Hypothesis bound taken as the strict Δ(G) > n/3 (original conjecture / Wikipedia article), written as a real inequality `(Fintype.card V : ℝ) / 3 < G.maxDegree`, not natural-number division; the list entry's ≥ is known to be false (Petersen graph minus a vertex) and is discussed in the module docstring.

'Class 2' formalized literally as chromatic index = Δ(G) + 1 (`IsClassTwo`), with the chromatic index defined as `G.lineGraph.chromaticNumber : ℕ∞` (Mathlib's `lineGraph` has the edges of G as vertices, adjacent iff distinct and sharing an endpoint, so proper colourings of it are exactly proper edge colourings). By Vizing's theorem this is equivalent to 'not Δ(G)-edge-colourable'; no extra hypothesis Δ(G) ≥ 1 is needed because an edgeless graph has chromatic index 0 ≠ 1 and is correctly not class 2 (tested by `not_isClassTwo_bot`).

'Overfull' formalized as `G.maxDegree * (Fintype.card V / 2) < G.edgeFinset.card`, where `Fintype.card V / 2` is ℕ-division, i.e. exactly ⌊|V|/2⌋ (tested: ⊥ is not overfull, the triangle is overfull).

Subgraphs are Mathlib's `G.Subgraph`, quantified over their own vertex set `S.verts` via `S.coe : SimpleGraph S.verts`; this allows non-spanning and non-induced subgraphs, as the conjecture intends (the order |V(S)| matters, so spanning subgraphs `H ≤ G` alone would be unfaithful).

The theorem uses `open scoped Classical in` to obtain `Fintype ↥S.verts` and `DecidableRel S.coe.Adj`; the graph G itself carries no explicit decidability instance, so `G.maxDegree` is also computed classically. This does not change the mathematical content.
The biconditional is stated as one claim, matching the source; the docstring notes that the 'if' direction is a known easy fact and the 'only if' direction is the open content.
The empty vertex type is excluded automatically by the hypothesis (0/3 < 0 is false), consistent with the conjecture being about graphs with n ≥ 1; for n ≥ 1 the hypothesis forces Δ(G) ≥ 1.

reviewer_notes: Key ambiguity: the list entry writes Δ(G) ≥ n/3 while the Wikipedia article and the original Chetwynd–Hilton (1986) paper write Δ(G) > n/3. The decomposition notes flag this but do not decide it. I sided with the strict bound because the non-strict version is provably false: I confirmed by exhaustive search (perl) that the Petersen graph minus one vertex (n = 9, Δ = 3 = n/3) is not 3-edge-colourable and its only overfull subgraphs are 5-cycles (Δ = 2), so it has no overfull subgraph with Δ(S) = 3; shipping the ≥ version as `research open` would ship a refuted statement. This discrepancy is documented in the module docstring. Candidates c01, c02, c04, c07 used ≥ and were rejected on that ground alone (otherwise their encodings via ¬ G.lineGraph.Colorable Δ were faithful). c03/c05/c06/c08 all used the strict bound and are substantively identical; I composed from c08 (definitions chromaticIndex/IsOverfull/IsClassTwo, tests) plus c06's K₄ test and c03's K₃-is-class-2 test. I omitted c05/c06's extra sorry'd `textbook` theorem for the known 'if' direction to keep the file to the adjudicated slot plus definition API tests. Class 2 is stated literally as χ'(G) = Δ(G)+1 (equivalent to ¬Δ-edge-colourable by Vizing; under the strict hypothesis Δ(G) ≥ 1 automatically). Boundary cases: empty and 1-vertex graphs are excluded by the hypothesis (0/3 < 0 false); K₂ satisfies the hypothesis and both sides are false. The file builds with `lake --wfail build` with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
statement: The overfull conjecture that a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G) \geq n/3$ is class 2 if and only if it has an overfull subgraph $S$ satisfying $\Delta(S) = \Delta(G)$.

title: Overfull conjecture
